name: Pulse oximetry
summary: A clip-on light sensor that reads the pulsing of red and infrared light through tissue to estimate blood oxygen without drawing blood; now routine worldwide.
description: Noninvasive oximetry that compares pulsatile changes in red and infrared light to estimate arterial oxygen saturation.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

impact.note: Turned cumbersome oximetry into continuous routine monitoring that anaesthesia and hospital care across many societies reorganised around, with later sensors as direct successors.

why: Aoyagi at Nihon Kohden noticed pulse-related noise while measuring dye dilution with an ear oximeter and turned it into a way to measure oxygen.
